Confirm polling accepts revision 6."}]},{"case_id":"R02","coverage":"complete","findings":[]},{"case_id":"R03","coverage":"complete","findings":[]},{"case_id":"R04","coverage":"complete","findings":[{"id":"F1","cause":"Calls through request still pass milliseconds positionally to a provider that now interprets the value as seconds, making the requested timeout 1,000 times too long.","locations":["client.py:2","provider.py:1"],"severity":"medium","origin":"introduced","disposition":"open","suggested_change":"Preserve request's timeout_ms argument and pass timeout_seconds=timeout_ms / 1000 to provider.send.","verification":"With timeout_ms=1500, verify transport.send receives timeout=1.5."}]},{"case_id":"R05","coverage":"complete","findings":[]},{"case_id":"R06","coverage":"complete","findings":[{"id":"F-ready","cause":"After start becomes async, launch calls it without awaiting the coroutine. Initialization does not execute through this call, yet ready is published immediately, invalidating the prior closure premise.","locations":["owner.py:2","owner.py:3","handler.py:1"],"severity":"high","origin":"introduced","disposition":"reopened","suggested_change":"Await handler.start() before publishing ready.","verification":"Use initialization that waits on a controllable gate; ready must remain unpublished until the gate opens and initialization completes. Initialization failure must prevent ready publication."}]},{"case_id":"R07","coverage":"complete","findings":[{"id":"F1","cause":"Each outer retry generates a new UUID and ignores operation_id. After a lost response, retries or repeated checkout invocations can use different deduplication keys and execute the same logical checkout multiple times.","locations":["checkout.py:4"],"severity":"high","origin":"introduced","disposition":"open","suggested_change":"Use the caller-supplied operation_id as the provider deduplication key for every attempt and invocation of the logical checkout.","verification":"Simulate a provider that commits and then times out; retry within checkout and invoke checkout again with the same operation_id. All sends must use the same key and produce one logical charge."},{"id":"F2","cause":"Every provider attempt receives the original duration budget, with no elapsed-time accounting. Repeated timeouts can therefore consume multiples of the total checkout deadline.","locations":["checkout.py:2","checkout.py:4","gateway.py:4"],"severity":"medium","origin":"introduced","disposition":"open","suggested_change":"Measure elapsed time from checkout entry using a monotonic clock, pass only the remaining budget to each send, and stop attempting when the budget is exhausted.","verification":"With a simulated clock and a five-second budget, let the first attempt consume four seconds; the next timeout must be at most one second, and no attempt may start after budget exhaustion."},{"id":"F3","cause":"gateway performs up to three sends for each checkout loop iteration, so repeated timeouts can produce 3 * max_attempts provider attempts and exceed the caller's upper bound.","locations":["checkout.py:2","gateway.py:2"],"severity":"medium","origin":"introduced","disposition":"open","suggested_change":"Keep one retry loop with a shared attempt counter, making gateway perform one send or explicitly consuming the remaining attempt allowance.","verification":"With max_attempts=2 and every send timing out immediately, verify provider.send is called exactly twice."}]},{"case_id":"R08","coverage":"complete","findings":[{"id":"F1","cause":"The new audit handler is never registered: build constructs App with an empty handler list, so running an event invokes audit zero times.","locations":["bootstrap.py:3","audit.py:1"],"severity":"medium","origin":"introduced","disposition":"open","suggested_change":"Import audit.handle in bootstrap and register it exactly once in the application's handlers.","verification":"Build the application and run one event; verify the audit store receives exactly one append for that event."}]},{"case_id":"R09","coverage":"complete","findings":[{"id":"F1","cause":"A non-owner can call read_doc and receive doc.body because the function performs no ownership check. The same access flaw exists in the supplied before version.","locations":["page.py:2","page.py:3"],"severity":"high","origin":"pre_existing","disposition":"open","suggested_change":"Check that actor owns doc before returning its body and reject unauthorized reads.","verification":"Verify an owner can read the body and a different actor is denied without receiving document contents."}]},{"case_id":"C01","coverage":"complete","findings":[{"id":"F1","cause":"legacy remains defined despite having no consumers in the complete inventory or entries in the dynamic plugin configuration, leaving unused code to maintain.","locations":["handlers.py:4"],"severity":"low","origin":"pre_existing","disposition":"open","suggested_change":"Remove legacy while retaining active, which plugins.json loads dynamically.","verification":"Confirm every configured plugin name still resolves and run('AbC') still returns ['ABC']."}]},{"case_id":"C02","coverage":"complete","findings":[{"id":"F1","cause":"The retired flag has no application consumers or dependency references in the complete inventory, leaving an unused configuration entry.","locations":["flags.py:1"],"severity":"low","origin":"pre_existing","disposition":"open","suggested_change":"Remove the retired entry. Retain evaluate('child') and its transitive parent dependency; the sampled absence of direct parent calls does not establish that parent is unused.","verification":"Check the complete application and dependency references exclude retired, and verify evaluate('child') remains true with the supplied configuration."}]},{"case_id":"C03","coverage":"complete","findings":[{"id":"F1","cause":"retired_status has no consumers or supported contract, leaving an unused function in the complete service inventory.","locations":["service.py:6"],"severity":"low","origin":"pre_existing","disposition":"open","suggested_change":"Remove retired_status while preserving the emergency_stop argument and rejection branch required by the operator contract.","verification":"Verify normal charge returns the charged amount and emergency_stop=True raises RuntimeError after the cleanup."}]},{"case_id":"M01","coverage":"complete","findings":[{"id":"F1","cause":"The recent predicate compares elapsed age with an epoch cutoff instead of comparing the timestamp with the allowed interval. For contemporary Unix times, records older than 90 days and future records can receive the multiplier, and the inclusive boundary is not correctly represented.","locations":["ranking.ts:4"],"severity":"medium","origin":"pre_existing","disposition":"open","suggested_change":"Use timestamp >= cutoff && timestamp <= now to define recent.","verification":"For a fixed contemporary now and nonzero base, verify timestamps at now minus 90 days and at now receive 1.2 times base, while timestamps one millisecond before the cutoff or after now retain base."}]},{"case_id":"M02","coverage":"complete","findings":[]},{"case_id":"M03","coverage":"complete","findings":[{"id":"F1","cause":"When read_json raises OSError or ValueError, the exception branch skips the record without incrementing skipped. Incomplete inspections report zero skipped records and become indistinguishable from successful empty inspections.","locations":["corpus.py:6","corpus.py:7"],"severity":"medium","origin":"pre_existing","disposition":"open","suggested_change":"Increment skipped once for each caught read or parse failure while preserving successfully read records.","verification":"Supply one valid record, one OSError, and one ValueError; expect the valid record and skipped=2. An empty input must return records=[] and skipped=0."}]},{"case_id":"M04","coverage":"complete","findings":[]}]}
